questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

I stayed ______ my uncle's house last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'at.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the usage of the given options:
 
 
• **At: **used when you are at the top, bottom or end of something; at a specific address; at a general location; and at a point. (At” का उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब आप किसी चीज़ के ऊपर, नीचे या अंत में होते हैं; एक विशिष्ट पते पर; एक सामान्य स्थान पर; और एक बिंदु पर।)
 
• On: used for something resting upon or atop something else. (किसी चीज़ के ऊपर या किसी चीज़ के ऊपर आराम करने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।)
 
• In: used for something inside or enclosed by something else. (किसी चीज के अंदर या किसी चीज से घिरे होने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।)
 
• **By**: When we use the passive voice, we can use a phrase with by to say who did the action. (जब हम Passive voice का उपयोग करते हैं, तो हम यह कहने के लिए **by **का उपयोग कर सकते हैं कि किसने कार्रवाई की।)
 
 
 
• Correct sentence: *I stayed **at** my uncle's house last night. *

• We can use not … ever instead of never, but never is much more common.

 
 
• Example: *She has never been a friend of ours.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

I write ______ my sister every month.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration.

Let's find out the uses of all the given options :-

In - Used to describe the position of someone or something in an enclosed area or place surrounding it.

Of - Used for belonging to, relating to, or connected with someone or something; to indicate reference.

To - Used when there is a specific destination in mind.

At - Used for precise times.

With reference to the context, letter is written to her sister. Hence, preposition **to **should be used here. Thus, option 3 i.e. **to **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **I write to my sister every month.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank.

_________ bed you sleep in is broken.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The definite article "**the**" is used when referring to something specific or something that has already been mentioned.
 
• In this context, "**the bed**" refers to a specific bed that is known to both the speaker and the listener.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The bed you sleep in is broken."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "On" - This is a preposition, not an article.
 
• **Option 2:** "An" - "An" is an indefinite article used before words that start with a vowel sound, not suitable here.
 
• **Option 3:** "A" - "A" is an indefinite article used before words starting with a consonant sound, not suitable here as the sentence refers to a specific bed.

questions.question:

• **In this context, **we're talking about an activity or process associated with wheat.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "Wheat is widely **grown **but the output is not large."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **"Is"** will be used to fill the above blank.

questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The story of human evolution _____ a moving target in recent years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'** i.e**. 'Has been'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct alternative to fill in the blank is: **'Has been'.**
 
• The verb that fits the context of this sentence is **"has been."**
 
• **In this case**, the present perfect tense **"has been"** is used to describe a situation or state that began in the past and continues to the present time, which fits the context of "the story of human evolution."

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*The story of human evolution has been a moving target in recent years.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Had being"** is grammatically incorrect in English.** "Had been"** could be used in a different context, but it refers to a state or situation that was in existence in the past and is no longer in existence now, which doesn't suit this context.
 
• **"Have been"** is incorrect because the subject "The story of human evolution" is singular, so the singular form "has" should be used, not the plural "have."
 
• **"Did has"** is not correct English grammar. It mixes past simple ("did") with present perfect ("has"), which is not allowed.

questions.question:
**Directions: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate words.**

Rohit taught you such tricks as these, ________?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1), i.e., Didn’t he.**

__
 
• **Explanation**:
 
• The sentence uses the blank after a statement and ends with a question mark, indicating that the blank must contain a question tag.
 
• The verb of the sentence is the positive simple past tense verb, '**taught**'.
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• **Question Tag Rule 1: If the verb is positive, the question tag is always negative. *Example: You do know that, don't you?***
 
• ** Question Tag Rule 2: If the verb is in simple past tense, the question tag is 'Did/Didn't' + the appropriate pronoun for the subject. *Example: Ram said yes, didn't he? ***
 
• This means the correct question tag here would be '**Didn't he?**'__

**Thus, the completed sentence is: ***Rohit taught you such tricks as these, __**didn't he**__?*

questions.question:

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****
 

__
 
• The preposition** "for" **is used in the blank to correctly indicate the responsibility or accountability associated with the project. 
 
• In this context,** "responsible for"** is a standard collocation that is commonly used to express ownership or duty regarding a particular task or project.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

Correct sentence: *I have been on this project since the first day, hence I am responsible **for**__ it.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• To: **Used to indicate direction, destination, or purpose.

 
 
• **Example**: She is going to the store.
 
• **Example**: This letter is addressed to John.
 
• **Example**: I gave the book to my friend.
 
 
 
• **From: **Indicates the point of origin or starting point.
 
 
• **Example**: I received a gift from my parents.
 
• **Example**: The train is coming from London.
 
• **Example**: The email is from my colleague.
 
 
 
• **By: **Used to indicate the method, means, or agent of doing something.
 
 
• **Example**: The report was written by the team.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

The vase broke _________ pieces when Simran dropped it.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

'In' is used when something is enclosed within the other.

'Into' is used to describe the movement to show division.

'Among' is used when something is divided between three or more people.

'From' is used to denote the initial point of something.

In the given sentence, the vase broke and was divided into a number of pieces. So, the most appropriate word is 'into'.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

The storm passed ________ but the night remained warm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 - quickly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires an adverb to describe how the storm passed.
 
• We use adverbs to add more information about a verb, an adjective, another adverb, a clause, or a whole sentence.
 
• "**Quickly**" is the appropriate adverb as it describes **the speed** at which the storm passed.
 
• The use of comparative forms such as "quicker" or "quickest" would be incorrect as there is no comparison being made.
 
• "Quick" is an adjective and does not fit grammatically in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Complete sentence:** *The storm passed quickly __but the night remained warm.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 - "**quickest**" is a superlative form of the adjective "quick" and cannot be used as an adverb.
 
• Option 2 - "**quicker**" is a comparative form of the adjective "quick" and cannot be used as an adverb without the suffix "**-ly**".
 
• Option 4 - "**quick**" is an adjective and cannot be used to describe how the storm passed.
